title: Separation of Fungal Extracellular Vesicles Using Ultracentrifugation
author: Piffer, Reis, et al.
materials: for high-throughput screening of EV production.
for facilitated approach yielding concentrated EV samples.

steps.title: Prepare media and buffers
steps.instruction: Prepare all required media and buffers for the workflow: YPD liquid, YPD agar, SD agar, and 1× PBS.

steps.title: Prepare iodixanol density gradient
steps.instruction: Make a 50 % (w/v) iodixanol stock, then prepare the gradient solutions (40 %, 20 %, 10 %, 5 %) as 7 mL each according to Table 1; assemble the stepwise gradient in Ultra‑clear tubes by sequentially adding 3 mL of 40 %, 3 mL of 20 %, 3 mL of 10 %, and 2.5 mL of 5 % iodixanol, freezing each layer at –80 °C for 20 min (freezing optional but must avoid mixing). Store the completed gradients at –20 °C (up to 1 week).

steps.title: High‑throughput EV isolation (Step 1a)
steps.instruction: Isolate EVs from many strains using a 96‑well deep‑well plate workflow.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑inoculum: add 1 mL liquid YPD to each well, inoculate with a loop of cells from a 48 h YPD agar plate (or add 20 µL frozen stock to 1 mL YPD), seal with breath‑seal and incubate 18 h at 30 °C with agitation.

Plate on SD‑agar: wash cells twice with sterile H₂O (centrifuge 3000 × g, 10 min; discard supernatant; resuspend in 1 mL H₂O, pipette up/down 10×; repeat twice), measure OD₆₀₀ of 200 µL, adjust to OD₆₀₀ = 0.4, spread 300 µL on SD‑agar plates, incubate 24 h at 30 °C (ensure plates are dry before spreading).

Collect cells & isolate EVs: scrape cells from agar into a sterile 2 mL tube containing 1 mL 0.22 µm‑filtered PBS (keep on ice), gently pipette to suspend (no vortex), optionally fix an aliquot with 4 % paraformaldehyde, centrifuge 7 000 × g, 5 min; transfer supernatant to a new 1.5 mL tube, centrifuge 11 000 × g, 5 min; filter supernatant through a 0.45 µm plate at 1 200 × g, 3 min, 4 °C; collect filtrate (contains EVs) and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Concentrated EV isolation (Step 1b)
steps.instruction: Obtain larger, concentrated EV preparations from agar plates.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑inoculum: inoculate 10 mL liquid YPD in a 50 mL flask with a loop of cells from a 48 h YPD plate, incubate 16–18 h at 30 °C with agitation.

Plate on SD‑agar: wash cells twice with sterile H₂O (collect 2 mL, centrifuge 11 000 × g, 3 min; discard supernatant; add 1 mL H₂O; repeat twice), count cells (e.g., Z1 Coulter counter with 100× dilution in Isoton II), dilute to 3.5 × 10⁷ cells mL⁻¹ in sterile H₂O, spread 300 µL on SD‑agar plates, incubate 24 h at 30 °C (dry plates before spreading; typically 6–12 plates are used).

Collect cells & isolate EVs: scrape up to 10 plates into 10 mL 0.22 µm‑filtered PBS in a sterile polypropylene bottle, keep on ice, gently pipette to suspend (no vortex), determine total volume and cell concentration, centrifuge 5 000 × g, 15 min, 4 °C; transfer supernatant to a new bottle, centrifuge 15 000 × g, 15 min, 4 °C; filter supernatant through a 0.45 µm syringe filter into an ultracentrifuge tube (SW41 Ti Ultra‑clear or 70 Ti polycarbonate), clean tubes per manufacturer (Extran 20 % detergent, rinse with MilliQ water, 70 % ethanol, air‑dry, final PBS washes), ultracentrifuge 100 000 × g, 1 h, 4 °C (max acceleration/deceleration), balance tubes, discard supernatant quickly, resuspend EV pellet in ≤300 µL 0.22 µm‑filtered PBS by pipetting 10–15 L times, aliquot and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Enrich EVs by iodixanol gradient (Step 2)
steps.instruction: Perform density‑gradient ultracentrifugation to enrich EV fractions.

substeps.instruction: Thaw a prepared iodixanol gradient at 4 °C for ≥3 h (do not use if not fully thawed).
Layer the EV sample (from Step 1b) on top of the gradient: suspend EVs in 500 µL PBS, keep 20 µL aside for quantification, add the remaining 480 µL onto the gradient.
Ultracentrifuge at 100 000 × g, 18 h, 4 °C using SW41 Ti rotor (max acceleration, deceleration set to 7).
Collect 12 fractions (F1–F12) by slowly pipetting 1 mL from top to bottom into new Ultra‑clear tubes (avoid mixing).
Dilute each fraction with 9 mL 0.22 µm‑filtered PBS, then ultracentrifuge each at 100 000 × g, 1 h, 4 °C (process up to 6 tubes at a time; keep remaining tubes on ice).
Discard supernatant by inverting tubes onto absorbent paper, then resuspend each pellet in 100 µL 0.22 µm‑filtered PBS by repeated pipetting.
Transfer resuspended fractions to sterile tubes and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Quantify EVs with NanoFCM (Part 1)
steps.instruction: Measure particle concentration and size using the NanoFCM Flow NanoAnalyzer.

substeps.instruction: Prepare reagents in 0.6 mL microcentrifuge tubes: 150 µL NanoFCM cleaning solution 1×; 150 µL 1 N NaOH (pre‑filtered 0.02 µm); 1 µL QC beads + 99 µL MilliQ water (1:100); 1 µL 68–155 nm sizing bead cocktail + 99 µL MilliQ water (1:100); 150 µL 0.02 µm‑filtered MilliQ water. Dilute QC and sizing beads fresh daily.
Start and align the NanoFCM per manufacturer: select Manual Operation → SPCM, load QC beads, boost 90 s, set Auto‑threshold to large signal, align laser optics.
Calibrate size: load sizing beads, boost 90 s, set Auto‑threshold to small signal, change SPCM correction SS sub value to 20.
Prepare blanks and samples diluted in TE buffer (10 mM Tris, 1 mM EDTA, pH 8, 0.02 µm‑filtered). Load TE buffer, boost 90 s, record blank.
For each sample: load diluted sample, boost 90 s, record (ensure 4000–13000 events; adjust dilution if outside range).
After all runs, clean the system by loading cleaning solution, boosting 90 s, then rinsing with MilliQ water.
Shutdown the instrument per instructions.

Data analysis: open NF Profession 2.0, load files, set concentration standard using QC beads (2.2 × 10¹⁰ beads mL⁻¹, dilution factor 100), set size standard with sizing beads (SS sub = 20, find peak), subtract TE buffer background (scale 200), apply sample dilution factors, export size and concentration results as PDF.

steps.title: Nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA) (Part 2)
steps.instruction: Determine EV concentration and size distribution using a Malvern Nanosight instrument.

substeps.instruction: Clean the NTA system: fill syringe with distilled water, attach to pump, flush 1 mL water three times; repeat cleaning between each sample.
Dilute EV samples in filter‑sterilized 0.22 µm PBS to a final concentration of 1 × 10⁸–1 × 10⁹ particles mL⁻¹.
Load diluted sample via 1 mL syringe onto the pump, set flow speed ≈50 µL min⁻¹.
Record three 60‑s videos per sample; set camera level 10–15, fluid viscosity to that of water, detection threshold 7–15.
Analyze videos with the NTA software (e.g., NTA 3.0) to obtain particle size distribution and concentration.

steps.title: Amplex Red cholesterol/ergosterol assay (Part 3)
steps.instruction: Measure sterol content of EVs using the Amplex Red fluorescence assay.

substeps.instruction: Prepare reagents per manufacturer; aliquot working solution and store at –20 °C (avoid repeated freeze‑thaw).

Generate a standard curve in a half‑area 96‑well black plate: add 25 µL of reaction buffer 1× to each well, then add 25 µL of cholesterol standards (serial two‑fold dilutions from 40 µM to 0 µM as in Table 2) to achieve final concentrations 40, 20, 10, 5, 2.5, 1.25, 0.625 µM.
Dilute EV samples directly in reaction buffer in the plate (e.g., for Step 1a samples, mix 10 µL EV sample + 15 µL 1× reaction buffer = 2.5‑fold dilution).
Start reactions by adding 25 µL of the Amplex Red working solution to each well, mix gently, avoid bubbles.
Incubate 30 min at 37 °C protected from light (wrap plate in aluminum foil).
Read fluorescence on a plate reader (e.g., TECAN Infinite 200) with excitation 560 nm, emission 590 nm; use the standard curve to calculate sterol concentration.

description: According to the latest Minimal information for studies of extracellular vesicles (MISEV 2023), extracellular vesicles (EVs) refer to particles that are released from cells, are delimited by a lipid bilayer, and cannot replicate on their own.5 Fungal EVs enclose diverse virulence factors, immunogens, and molecules with unknown functions, mediating biofilm formation, contributing to antifungal resistance, and stimulating host immune responses.6 To better understand the fungal EV biosynthetic processes, their biomarkers, and multiple biological roles, the protocol for EV isolation from solid culture media has proven to be a suitable method. The techniques outlined below have been designed to separate, enrich, and characterize the biophysical and biochemical properties of EVs originating from the fungus Cryptococcus neoformans. It is worth noting that this protocol can be adapted to isolate EVs from other fungal species. To achieve this, carefully considering the appropriate growth condition is essential, tailored to the specific organism being studied.
